race_context: Blue River Valley Schools is based in Mount Summit in northern Henry County and serves Blue River and Prairie townships; its elementary and junior-senior high schools sit on one campus {wiki_brvhs}{ct_ae24}. State enrollment counts were 642 students in 2022-23, 614 in 2023-24, 620 in 2024-25 and 618 in 2025-26, down from 832 in 2005-06 {idoe_enroll}.

Superintendent: Lori Dickerson, formerly the district's junior-senior high principal, elementary principal and assistant superintendent, was hired after Trent McCormick resigned effective June 30, 2024 {ct_mcc24}{ct_bigplans24}{ct_localsup24}. She was still superintendent in January 2026 {ct_meetkids26}.

The board has five members, all elected at large {ct_ae24}{hc_2022_results}{hc_2024_results}. In 2022 voters filled two at-large seats (Ashley Beavers 847 votes and incumbent Brian Koontz 785, over Travis Estes 314, Terry DeWayne Coffey 229 and Jeffrey Alan Denney 178) {hc_2022_results}{ct_hometown22}. In 2024 voters filled three (Carla Bryant 1,100, Mysia Brown 1,068 and Lance Brown 1,014, over Tina Moore 854 and Celeste Wright-Black 361) {hc_2024_results}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: the two at-large seats won in 2022. The state list shows the race as 'At Large 2' with 'vote for 1', but the Henry County candidate list published by The Courier-Times says 'Vote for not more than two candidates', so the top two of the three candidates will be elected {in_list}{ct_cands26}. Incumbent Ashley Beavers is running again; Brian Koontz, who won the other seat in 2022, is not on the 2026 candidate list, so at least one of the two seats will go to a newcomer {ct_cands26}{hc_2026_list}. This guide could not read 2025-26 board records to confirm the current roster.

Party labels: Rich King and Katharine N. (Nikki) Koontz are listed as Republicans; Ashley Beavers is listed with no party {hc_2026_list}{ct_cands26}. In 2022 no Blue River Valley candidate was listed with a party {hc_2022_results}.

Teacher pay and the 2024 referendum: in spring 2024 the board asked voters for a $0.19 operating tax levy increase to raise teacher pay. Then-superintendent McCormick said BRV's starting teacher pay ranked last among area districts and its average teacher salary was $8,500 below the state average {ct_brvref24}. Voters rejected it in May 2024 {ct_localsup24}. In his June 2024 resignation notice McCormick said the referendum was 'necessary for our district but difficult for the community' {ct_mcc24}. In December 2024 Dickerson said 'We failed a referendum horribly' and, as the newspaper reported it, that seven of 13 current Blue River teachers were new {ct_localsup24}.

Budget and state funding (2025-2026): at a Jan. 15, 2026 Chamber of Commerce panel on the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1) and state cuts, Dickerson said the district had lost $17,000 in six months, mainly from reduced child-care voucher payments for its pre-K, and was weighing whether pre-K is sustainable {ct_meetkids26}. This guide found no BRV-specific estimate of SEA 1's effect.

Facilities: in January 2023 McCormick said two long-term bonds would be paid off in the next few years, letting the district borrow for building projects, with the elementary building the main focus, 'without changing the tax rate' {ct_brvplan23}. After the 2024 election Bryant said she most looked forward to completing BRV's capital projects {ct_ae24}.
School safety: in September 2026 BRV received a $43,000 state Secured School Safety matching grant {ct_safety26}.

Academics and programs: Dickerson has said BRV offers graduation pathways in biomedical, agriculture, business and computer science, and a weekly 'Wednesday Works' program for all K-12 students {ct_bigplans24}{ct_meetkids26}.

Forums: this guide found no 2026 candidate forum, questionnaire or campaign website for any Blue River Valley candidate. The district website blocked automated access, so 2025-26 board minutes could not be read.
